content:
incident-bot: 🚨 AUTOSCALER_ALERT: Pool 'gpu-ap-southeast3' failed to scale due to quota/alloc error. 85% queue growth in last 5m. More details: https://internal.redwood/alerts/2623456789

sara_oncall: got the page, reading logs now. panicked? not yet.

mike_infra: I'm seeing repeated 403s from cloud API: 
```
E0421 14:12:03 autoscaler.go:214] failed to create instance: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project 12345 in region asia-southeast3. The request failed with status code 403.
```
Looks like region-level GPU quota hit. autoscaler retried 5x then backed off.

lina_sre: queue length spiking to ~4200 waiting tasks, p50 latency > 1200ms, p95 > 4s. some customers reporting errors 429 / 503 in front-end.

jamie_prod: Customer-impact: two mid-market customers on dedicated pools in ap-southeast are showing degraded throughput. CS alerted their CSMs.

sara_oncall: tagging @mike_infra @lina_sre — what options fast? can we fallback to CPU-backed inference? or smaller model variants?

mike_infra: immediate options: 1) failover to another region (ap-southeast2) — needs routing switch and possibly higher latency. 2) enable burst from shared hosted pool (requires approval, but can be toggled). 3) temporary model downscale: route requests to quantized-8bit variants to reduce GPU pressure.

lina_sre: I'll flip autoscaler to allow fallback policy to 'region-failover' and enable model-variant fallback for affected routes. Doing a canary redirect for 5% first.

sara_oncall: do it. please paste commands you run.

mike_infra: running command to enable hosted-burst for this customer tag:
```
# enable burst (internal tool)
redwood infra burst-allow --region asia-southeast3 --pool gpu-ap-southeast3 --duration 2h --reason "autoscale quota hit"
```
Response: queued for approval (automated throttles). manual override required.

jamie_prod: if manual override needed, who can approve? ops-leads?

mike_infra: @lina_sre or @sara_oncall can approve in the console; doing it now.

lina_sre: approved, burst override applied. Confirming token allocations.

eng-ml-bot: Model fallback config applied for routes: /v1/generate (customers: cust-142, cust-78). Fallback -> model-redwood-medium-8q.

sara_oncall: rolling 5% traffic failover -> 20% -> 50%. monitor.

lina_sre: after 2 minutes: queue length decreased from 4200 -> 1500. p95 latency down to 2.3s. errors dropping.

customer-success: CSMs notified; they've acknowledged and updated customers with brief status. No customer-facing incident page published yet.

mike_infra: parallel path: filing expedited quota increase with Azure support. Created ticket AZ-123456. ETA unknown but requested 4 GPU units. Ticket body: "Project 12345, region asia-southeast3, request temporary quota increase of NVIDA A100 GPUs by 8 units for 2 hours due to autoscaler failures causing customer impact. Contact: mike_infra@redwood.com"

sara_oncall: good. keep both mitigations in parallel. If burst expires before quota comes in, we'll need to failover region for remaining traffic.

lina_sre: quick note — autoscaler logs show backoff loop: 
```
W0421 14:13:11 autoscaler.go:312] backoff: rate limit for API requests reached, will retry in 30s
E0421 14:13:41 autoscaler.go:214] create instance failed: quota exceeded
E0421 14:14:11 autoscaler.go:214] create instance failed: quota exceeded
```
We should add a mitigation to stop aggressive retry to conserve quota tokens. Changing retry multiplier to 1.5.

mike_infra: changed retry ramp to conservative. Also enabled instance preemption tolerance to accept smaller VMs temporarily.

jamie_prod: any chance that some user traffic is routing to dedicated pools in other regions unexpectedly? trying to understand blast radius.

lina_sre: blast radius limited to services with region tag ap-southeast3 and routes pinned to that pool. we have ~12 jobs in other regions affected only if we do failover.

sara_oncall: short summary for pager: cause = Azure region GPU quota exhausted; autoscaler retries hit quota and backed off; effect = queue growth + client 429/503 for some customers; mitigations = enabled hosted-burst override, applied model fallback to quantized variant, slowed autoscaler retries, filed expedited quota increase, prepared region failover as fallback.

customer-success: please confirm whether to send proactive email to impacted customers now or wait until we have stable metrics.

jamie_prod: send a short proactive note: "We're aware of degraded throughput in AP-SE3 for some workloads; we've activated burst capacity and temporary fallbacks to reduce errors. We'll update in 1h or when resolved." Keep it technical-light.

lina_sre: monitoring shows errors now down 70% since mitigation. queue trending down to 600.

mike_infra: Azure ticket updated with logs. Support assigned to L2. They asked for exact project/fingerprint; sent.

sara_oncall: timeline notes for postmortem: 1) why autoscaler retried aggressively instead of stopping 2) consider proactive quota monitoring and automated failover thresholds 3) consider reserving cross-region warm capacity for key customers 4) improve runbook on burst approval process so override doesn't need manual click.

lina_sre: agreed. Will start draft of action items.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity reduced to S2. Next update scheduled in 30m.

sara_oncall: I'll keep watch for another 30m then hand off to next on-call. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jamie_prod: follow-up: CS sent email to two impacted customers. No escalations so far.

customer-success: confirmed both customers acknowledged and appreciate the quick update.

lina_sre: marking mitigation stable. moving thread to postmortem channel after resolution.

sara_oncall: last note: keep quotas inroad dashboard on watch and set alert at 80% region GPU consumption.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Queue returned to baseline, autoscaler resumed normal operations. Closing thread."
